instruction.name: str.w
instruction.description: store right part of a value to an unaligned 32-bit address

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 2000 --unroll2 8000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 10 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; st.d $r0, $r20, 0; st.d $r0, $r20, 8; st.d $r0, $r20, 16; st.d $r0, $r20, 24; li.d $r12, 0' --asm 'str.w $r4, $r20, 0; str.w $r5, $r20, 0; str.w $r6, $r20, 0; str.w $r7, $r20, 0; str.w $r8, $r20, 0; str.w $r9, $r20, 0; str.w $r10, $r20, 0; str.w $r11, $r20, 0'
throughput.notes: Store: latency not measured, it depends on cache state; the throughput is 0.5 CPI when the buffer is aligned, like `st.d`, and 1 CPI for the left-part forms.

notes: LBT MIPS-style unaligned store, measured with a 64-byte-aligned zeroed stack buffer. Latency is not recorded because a store has no register result.
